Choose, digitize and check photographs: the measuring hub

Source: R/measure_hub.R
launch_measure_hub.Rd

Launches the screen that comes before digitize_landmarks() and the one that comes after it, for any folder of photographs.

Usage

launch_measure_hub(
  photo_dir = NULL,
  xlsx_path = NULL,
  journal_dir = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  operator = NULL,
  ruler_mm = 10,
  mlmorph_dir = NULL,
  python = NULL,
  levels = c("Folder", "Sub-folder"),
  traits_fun = NULL,
  apps = NULL,
  default_apps = TRUE,
  sync_fun = NULL,
  literature = NULL,
  title = "intraitR - measure",
  launch.browser = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

photo_dir

Root folder of the photographs (sub-folders included). NULL (default): the hub opens on a start page where the folder is chosen (or photographs are uploaded into a new one), with the species, where the measurements are saved, the operator and the ruler – and the recent sessions, reopened in one click. Open another folder, on the home page of the hub, comes back to it.

xlsx_path

Workbook written by the digitizer. NULL: intraitR_landmarks.xlsx next to photo_dir, as digitize_landmarks().

journal_dir

Landmark journal. NULL: landmark_journal next to the workbook.

species

Where the species come from: NULL, "folder" (one folder per species) or a table; see measure_queue(). Also a function without argument returning such a table, called again at every refresh (so that photographs imported while the hub is open get their species).

operator

Operator identifier (editable in the hub). NULL: the system user.

ruler_mm

Real distance between landmarks 20 and 21, in mm (editable).

mlmorph_dir, python

ml-morph folder and Python interpreter, as in digitize_landmarks() (editable).

levels

Labels of the two folder levels in the hub, e.g. c("Site", "Date") or c("Species", "Sub-folder").

traits_fun

Optional function computing the trait table, called as traits_fun(codes, xlsx_path, ruler_mm, scale_action) with the photograph codes to keep; it must return a data.frame with a column specimen_code (and may return photo_code and species). NULL uses read_landmarks_xlsx(), fishmorph_segments() and fishmorph_ratios(). This is how a data-management layer attaches its own metadata.

apps

Other applications the hub opens, each in its own background R process and browser tab, so that the hub is the one place a session starts from. A list of entries list(label = , fun = "pkg::launcher", args = list(...), place = ), place being "select" (a button of the Select tab: importing data, for example), "photo" (a button on one photograph, in the gallery magnifier and in the Annotated photograph tab; its code is passed in the argument named photo_arg; warn_measured is shown first when the photograph is already measured; close_digitizer = TRUE closes an open digitizer first, for an application that rewrites the workbook; photo_query: the URL parameter the application reads the photograph from, so that an open application is pointed at the next photograph in its own tab instead of being restarted) or "menu" (the Apps menu only; every non-photograph application is in that menu). The launcher must pass ... to shiny::runApp(). The hub refreshes its photographs when one of these applications closes.

default_apps

Add the FISHMORPH functional space (Rfishmorph::launch_fishmorph_space()) to the Apps menu.

sync_fun

Optional function without argument, run by the hub's Save to the database button, when the digitizer closes and at Finish: what a data-management layer needs to register the measurements (for FishInTrait, linking the workbook's specimens in the project manifest). It returns a short message, shown in the hub. The landmarks themselves need no such step: each Save & next of the digitizer writes them to the journal at once.

literature

Optional individual trait records that have no photograph – published data sets, typically: a data.frame, or a function without argument returning one (called when needed), with a column species, the nine FISHMORPH ratios (BEl ... CPt) and optionally site, date, study_id, specimen_code. They appear in the Results page under the provenance "literature" (one filter per study), in its Traits table, and in the analyses it opens (launch_intrait_analyses()) for every analysis based on the ratios. FishInTrait passes the literature of the project.

title

Title shown in the hub.

launch.browser

Where the hub opens; see digitize_landmarks().

...

Passed to shiny::runApp().

Value

Invisibly, when closed with Finish, a list: photo_dir, xlsx_path, journal_dir, selected (the selected photographs, as in measure_queue()) and traits (the last table computed, or NULL). NULL when the hub is stopped otherwise.

Details

  1. Setup: paths, operator, ruler, ml-morph folder; the sub-folders with their numbers of photographs and of measured ones.

  2. Select: a folder and a sub-folder (for example a site and a date, or a species), a gallery of their photographs with species and measured state, a species table; any subset can be picked (a species, the photographs not yet measured, a few by hand).

  3. Digitize: optionally the automatic pre-pass batch_landmarks() (with or without a ruler on the photographs), then digitize_landmarks() on exactly the selection. The digitizer runs in a separate R process and opens in its own browser tab; the hub stays usable.

  4. Results: progress by folder and species; landmarks and their statuses (clicked, predicted, seeded...) read from the journal, with its quality control; the FISHMORPH traits (a specimen without a ruler keeps its nine ratios, its segments then being in pixels); any photograph with its landmarks drawn on it, and a Remeasure button that reopens the digitizer on that photograph alone, in correct mode. The tables follow the journal while the digitizer is running.

Finish (top right) stops the digitizer and the pre-pass if they are running – the digitizer is interrupted cleanly, which writes its workbook – closes the hub and returns to the console.

See also

measure_queue(), digitize_landmarks(), batch_landmarks()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# one folder per species, a 10 mm ruler on the photographs
# no argument: choose everything on the start page
res <- launch_measure_hub()

res <- launch_measure_hub("~/my_photos", species = "folder",
                          levels = c("Species", "Sub-folder"),
                          operator = "XX", mlmorph_dir = "~/ml_morph")
res$traits
} # }
